claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct that is enforced entirely within Pulumi.
The Pulumi `protect` resource option is never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own, separate deletion-protection attributes, such as `deletionProtection` on a GCP Cloud SQL instance.
An AWS RDS instance has a `deletionProtection` deletion-protection attribute.
Cloud-provider deletion-protection attributes such as `deletionProtection` are enforced by the cloud provider independently of anything Pulumi knows about (including Pulumi's `protect` option).

A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi (`protect` not set) and still refuse to delete because of a provider-side deletion-protection attribute, or vice versa (protected in Pulumi but not protected by the cloud provider).

The page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' (anchor #deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself) explaining how to tell Pulumi `protect` and provider-side deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option guards a resource within Pulumi only (Pulumi refuses to delete it), and is separate from any deletion protection enforced by the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` option, which the provider or the cloud API enforces independently of Pulumi.

A GCP Cloud SQL instance resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute (Pulumi property name `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance`) that provides deletion protection independent of Pulumi's `protect` option.

An AWS RDS instance resource has a `deletionProtection` attribute (Pulumi property `deletionProtection` on `aws.rds.Instance`) that provides deletion protection independent of Pulumi's `protect` option.
Pulumi's `protect` option and a cloud resource's own deletion-protection attributes are complementary layers rather than substitutes for one another.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section titled 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' (anchor #deletion-protection-on-the-resource-itself).

The 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' section of the destroy-failures troubleshooting page explains how to tell Pulumi's `protect` apart from resource-level deletion protection and how to resolve a destroy failure caused by either.

Protection against deletion that causes `pulumi destroy` failures can be held in three distinct layers (Pulumi's `protect` option, a provider-enforced flag, a cloud-API-enforced protection), and the error message usually indicates which layer was hit.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
When `pulumi destroy` fails because of the `protect` resource option, the error names a URN and mentions `protect`.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` resource option.
Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call at all when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the Pulumi provider.
For provider-enforced deletion protection, the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
Some clouds reject the delete call themselves, independent of Pulumi, for example via AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, or an Azure Resource Manager management lock.
For cloud-API-enforced deletion protection, the error text comes back from the cloud provider's API, often with a distinct error code such as `ScopeLocked` (Azure management lock).
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is already recorded in the stack's state, not what the Pulumi program currently says.
Setting a deletion-protection attribute to `false` in the Pulumi program is not enough on its own to make `pulumi destroy` succeed.
The remediation for provider-enforced and cloud-API-enforced deletion protection is the same.

To remove provider- or cloud-enforced deletion protection: set the attribute to `false` in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches both the live resource and Pulumi's state, then run `pulumi destroy`.

If deletion protection was already disabled outside of Pulumi (e.g., in the cloud console), `pulumi refresh` synchronizes the stack's state with reality, and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a `deletionProtection` attribute that is provider-enforced.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute.
Destroying a `gcp.bigquery.Dataset` that still contains tables fails unless `deleteContentsOnDestroy` is `true`.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API.
`deletionProtection` on `aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` defaults to `false`.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to `false`.
A non-empty `aws.s3.BucketV2` fails to delete unless `forceDestroy` is true.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute (EC2 termination protection) that is enforced by the AWS API.
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute that is enforced by the AWS API.
`deletionProtectionEnabled` on `aws.dynamodb.Table` defaults to `false`.
`azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and its scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist as Pulumi resources for Azure management locks.
Azure management locks are enforced by Azure Resource Manager, and a `CanNotDelete` lock must be removed before the locked resource can be deleted, independent of anything in the Pulumi program.
Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it.
Recreating an Azure Key Vault with the same name as a soft-deleted vault fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered.
Azure Key Vault purge protection prevents purging a soft-deleted vault until its retention period elapses.
